body_markdown:
*Embedder joins the organization behind the open ISA to help chip vendors, and the teams building on their silicon, get RISC-V products to market faster.*


**SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 21, 2026**


Embedder, an AI startup building the world's first autonomous firmware engineer, today announced that it has joined RISC-V International as a Strategic Member.


RISC-V is an open, royalty-free instruction set architecture (ISA). Instead of licensing a proprietary architecture, chipmakers can implement the RISC-V standard and extend it to fit their needs. RISC-V International, a non-profit, maintains the specifications and coordinates the global community of companies, universities, and developers that advance them.[Learn more about RISC-V](https://riscv.org/about/) .


That openness is moving RISC-V out of research and into mainstream embedded products. In 2025,[Infineon announced](https://www.infineon.com/press-release/2025/infatv202503-067) a RISC-V-based automotive microcontroller family under its AURIX brand, the first automotive RISC-V MCU family from any semiconductor supplier. Similar moves across IoT, industrial, and edge computing mean more firmware teams will be writing code for RISC-V cores in the coming years.


A new architecture brings new work for those teams. RISC-V is modular, so each chip implements its own combination of the base ISA and optional extensions, and many vendors add custom extensions on top. Interrupt controllers, startup code, linker scripts, and toolchain settings all differ from what engineers are used to on Arm Cortex-M. Debugging relies on the RISC-V debug specification rather than familiar vendor tooling. Porting an existing codebase means working through each of these details, then confirming that the result behaves correctly on hardware.


Embedder is built for this kind of work. Its agent helps engineers understand existing firmware, make code changes, and work through build and debug cycles. Through supported debug probes, Embedder connects directly to target hardware, so it can flash builds, inspect device state, and investigate runtime failures. That shortens the path from a code change to working firmware, whatever the architecture.


This matters on both sides of the RISC-V ecosystem. For chip vendors, a new RISC-V part succeeds only when customers can build on it quickly, and software and tooling are often the bottleneck. Embedder helps close that gap by making engineers productive on new silicon from day one. For device makers building on those chips, Embedder speeds up board bring-up, porting, and debugging, so teams can move to RISC-V without stalling their roadmaps. The result is faster time to market for vendors and their customers alike.


Through RISC-V International's technical and community groups, Embedder will bring the firmware developer's perspective to the ecosystem, along with hands-on insight into AI-assisted development. Embedder looks forward to working with the community to help more RISC-V products reach the market.
